title: The Room Next Door
sections: Verse 1
Forty years I could walk this whole house in the dark
I could find every door, I could feel every stair
then I heard you get up with that little tired sigh
and I came with the tea and you weren't in your chair
Chorus 1
It's the north wall, love, but it's warm to my hand
like the sun's coming in where the sunlight never falls
you're just in the room next door
and I can't come yet, but I'm not shut out at all
there's a door in the wall
Verse 2
I have kept your cup and your book on the stand
lying open face down at the page you were on
and I moved my own chair to the cold north wall
and I sit there at night when the day is gone
Chorus 2
It's the north wall, love, but it's warm to my hand
like the sun's coming in where the sunlight never falls
you're just in the room next door
and I can't come yet, but I'm not shut out at all
there's a door in the wall
Verse 3
Margaret came in the spring with her bags and her worry
and she watched me the way that daughters do
and I said hello through the plaster that night
and I slept the whole night through, the first time since you
Bridge
One morning early, the light coming in
my hand on the wall and the kettle not on
the room next door came as close as a breath
and you were there, and the wall was all but gone
Verse 4
I made us two cups and we sat on the stair
and she said Mama, you look more than slept
and I said there's a door, and it's going to open
and I know who'll be there when I take the step
Last Chorus
It's the north wall, love, and it's warm to my hand
like the sun's coming in where the sunlight never falls
and some morning it opens and I'll walk through
and the first thing I'll know is you, after all
there's a door in the wall
there's a door in the wall
